title: The surah that turned him gray
hookLine: the Prophet ﷺ said Hud and its sisters had turned his hair gray (Tirmidhi)

cards: Abu Bakr looked at his friend one day and noticed something. A few white hairs in the beard. Not many.

Anas, who served the Prophet for years, said later that at the end of his life there weren't even twenty white hairs on his head and beard together. But Abu Bakr saw them, and said so: Messenger of God, you've gone gray.
The answer he got is why this lesson starts Surah Hud here. Not with a story, though Hud is full of stories. With a confession of how heavy these words were to carry.

teach.b: At-Tirmidhi records the answer. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: Hud turned me gray, and al-Waqi'ah, and al-Mursalat, and 'Amma yatasa'alun, and Idha ash-shamsu kuwwirat. Hud and its sisters.
Look at what they share. The four sisters are shorter surahs, in the later part of the Qur'an, about the Day the sun is folded up, the stars fall and every soul sees what it did.
Hud is long, the eleventh surah, and it tells, one after another, the stories of prophets and their peoples: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb, Musa.
Ending after ending. Scholars have asked: what exactly in Hud weighed on him?
One answer, reported from Ibn 'Abbas, points to a single verse, one hundred twelve: so stand firm, as you have been commanded, you and those who turn with you, and don't overstep.
Ibn 'Abbas is reported to have said that no verse was harder on the Prophet than that one.

teach.h: HE FELT IT IN HIS BODY.
teach.b: It's not a threat. It's a command to keep going straight, every day, without drifting, and to carry others with you. Elsewhere the Qur'an tells him it will lay on him a weighty word.
These surahs are weighty words. Some readers find this hadith a comfort. The Prophet didn't read the Qur'an lightly.
He felt it in his body, down to a few white hairs.

how: Teachers of Qur'an recitation often cite the hadith 'Hud and its sisters turned me gray' to encourage slow, attentive recitation, and some Muslims read Surah Hud with special seriousness.

games.q: Abu Bakr says: you've gone gray. what does the Prophet answer, in at-Tirmidhi's hadith?
o: Hud and its sisters turned me gray.
games.why: Hud and its sisters. he felt the weight of the surahs about the end of peoples and the Last Day.

practice: Take one line: so stand firm, as you have been commanded. Say it slowly in your head, one phrase per breath, letting each phrase land, and notice where in your life it's hard to keep going straight.
If you pray, you can sit with the verse in Arabic or in your own language.

wordCard.voice: Hud. The surah that the Prophet said, with its sisters, had turned his hair gray. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "so stand firm, as you have been commanded" (11:112), the verse Ibn 'Abbas called the hardest on him.

carryVoice: Your line: weighty words. Some words are meant to be carried slowly. Day four hundred thirty-three, counted.
